title: Fonio Salad with Lemon and Mint
author: Pierre Thiam
desc: Steamed fonio dressed with a lemon-oil vinaigrette and parsley, mint, cucumber and plum tomatoes — in Thiam’s own first-person account of finding fonio in Senegal.
longDesc: From the face2faceafrica article ‘A Chef’s Journey: In Search of Fonio in Senegal’, byline Pierre Thiam, 1 April 2014. A cup of fonio is washed in cold running water, drained and steamed in a cheesecloth-lined steamer about 15 minutes, fluffed, sprinkled with salted water and steamed again until tender; the page also offers a microwave method, in a bowl with enough water to cover, 6–8 minutes. The vinaigrette is the juice of two lemons, salt and pepper with a cup of oil whisked in slowly to emulsify. The fonio is tossed with parsley, mint, cucumber and tomatoes and dressed enough to coat the grains.
ingredients: 1 tbsp salt dissolved in 1/4 cup water
1 cup peanut or canola oil (the method says ‘olive oil’ — see sources)
steps: Wash the fonio with cold running water and drain well. Place it in the top of a steamer lined with cheesecloth and steam about 15 minutes. Fluff, sprinkle with the salted water and steam again until the grains are tender. Alternatively microwave it in a bowl with enough water to cover, until tender, 6–8 minutes.
Whisk the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Slowly whisk in the oil to emulsify.
Combine the cooked fonio with the parsley, mint, cucumber and tomatoes. Add enough dressing to coat the grains well, toss and serve.
chefTips: ‘Steam again until the grains are tender’ is the doneness cue; the first steam is a time (about 15 minutes).
Add enough dressing ‘to coat the grains well’ — no more.
The page’s salted water is 1 tbsp in 1/4 cup.
The oil mismatch in the page (peanut or canola in the list, olive in the method) is recorded; use whichever you have.
healthBenefits: Fresh herbs, cucumber and tomato add vitamins.
culturalNote: One of only two recipes in the Senegal research bylined to Thiam personally and written in the first person. The article is about his search for fonio in Senegal.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Fonio Salad (vegan, gluten-free)’, inside ‘A Chef’s Journey: In Search of Fonio in Senegal’. Byline: ‘BY Pierre Thiam, 11:48am April 01, 2014’. Publication: face2faceafrica.com. Yield: none printed (4 used here). TWO-PASS on every quantity.
ingredients transcribed with the page’s irregular abbreviations (‘1-cup fonio’, ‘1Tbs.’, ‘ts.’, ‘c.’, ‘1/4c’), reported as printed and normalised here only for readability.
INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, FLAGGED, TWO-PASS: the ingredient list specifies ‘peanut or canola oil’ but step two says to pour in ‘the olive oil’. Not reconciled.
No temperatures. Cues in short fragments: ‘until the grains are tender’; ‘until tender, 6–8 minutes’; ‘to emulsify’; ‘to coat the grains well’.
Compare SEN062 (Thiam’s WBUR mango fonio salad) which uses 1 cup of olive oil with 2 lemons for 2 cups of cooked fonio; this one 1 cup of dry fonio, 1 cup of oil.
